documents.content:

Late payments: Invoices unpaid after 30 days accrue interest at 1% per month.
Revisions: Two rounds of revisions included in all project quotes. Additional rounds: $150/round.
Project holds: Client-caused delays of more than 14 days may result in a restart fee of $300.

This policy applied to all projects initiated before March 15, 2025 unless a separate contract specifies otherwise.

documents.title: School Medication Policy – Version 1 (Superseded)
documents.content:
NORTHGATE PRIMARY SCHOOL
Administration of Medication Policy – Effective Term 1 2023

Parents wishing to have medication administered during school hours must complete a Medication Authority Form and provide the original labelled container. Medication must be brought to the front office by a parent or guardian; students may not carry medication. The school will store all medication in the locked first-aid cabinet. This policy is reviewed annually.

Note: Asthma inhalers may be held by students in Year 5 and above only.

[SUPERSEDED – see updated policy issued Feb 2024]

documents.title: School Medication Policy – Version 2 (Current)
documents.content:
NORTHGATE PRIMARY SCHOOL
Administration of Medication Policy – Effective 5 February 2024

Parents wishing to have medication administered during school hours must complete a Medication Authority Form and supply medication in its original labelled container. Medication is to be delivered to the front office by a parent or guardian. Students may not self-carry medication except as detailed below.

Updated provision: Students in Year 3 and above with a current Asthma Action Plan on file may carry a reliever inhaler on their person during school hours and excursions. All other medications remain in the locked first-aid cabinet.

Reviewed and approved by Principal D. Hargreaves, 5 Feb 2024.

documents.title: Letter: GP Referral – Mia Brennan
documents.content:
Dr Yuen Lim
Sunrise Medical Centre, 204 Fenwick Rd, Footscray VIC 3011
3rd April 2024

Dear Dr Callahan,

I am referring Mia Brennan (DOB 12/07/2016) for a paediatric audiology assessment. Mia's mother reports intermittent difficulty hearing in classroom settings over the past three months. There is no history of recurrent ear infections. Mia's last full hearing screen was conducted at school in June 2022 and was within normal limits at that time.

I would be grateful for your review and any recommended follow-up.

Yours sincerely,
Dr Yuen Lim
MBBS FRACGP

Wednesday 8 May 2024 at 9:30 am

Please bring the GP referral letter and Medicare card. Allow approximately 90 minutes. Call us on (03) 9689 5500 if you need to rearrange.

Thanks,
Soundclear Admin

documents.title: Mandatory Overtime Policy – Ward 7 (REVISED Feb 2025)
documents.content:
Effective February 1, 2025. This revision supersedes the policy dated October 2023.

Mandatory overtime may be assigned when ward census exceeds 90% capacity and fewer than two relief nurses are available. Staff will receive no less than 4 hours' notice before a mandatory overtime shift. Overtime is compensated at 1.5× the employee's base hourly rate. Employees may decline mandatory overtime a maximum of twice per rolling 12-month period without formal documentation. A third refusal triggers a meeting with the unit manager. Questions: contact HR ext. 214.

documents.title: Mandatory Overtime Policy – Ward 7 (OLD – October 2023) [SUPERSEDED]
documents.content:
Effective October 15, 2023. Superseded February 2025 – do not apply.

Mandatory overtime may be assigned at charge nurse discretion when staffing falls below safe ratios. Staff will receive no less than 2 hours' notice. Overtime is compensated at 1.5× base rate. Employees may decline mandatory overtime once per 12-month period; a second refusal triggers a formal meeting. This version is retained for audit purposes only.

documents.title: Venue Booking Confirmation – Elmhurst Estate
documents.content:
Hi Priya and Tom,

Great news — we're delighted to confirm your booking at Elmhurst Estate for Saturday, 14 June 2025. The ceremony will begin at 2:00 pm, with the reception to follow in the main barn through to midnight. We have you down for a maximum of 120 guests.

Your deposit of £1,500 was received on 3rd March 2025 and the remaining balance of £3,200 is due no later than 30 days before the event. Please quote reference EE-0442 in all correspondence.

Warm regards,
Sarah Okonkwo
Elmhurst Estate Events

documents.title: Elmhurst Estate – Damage & Cancellation Policy (Updated April 2025)
documents.content:
Effective 1 April 2025 this policy supersedes all previous versions.

Cancellation: Cancellations made more than 90 days before the event date receive a 50% refund of the deposit. Cancellations within 90 days forfeit the deposit in full.

Damage: Clients are liable for any damage to the venue, fixtures, or grounds caused by guests or third-party suppliers. A refundable damage bond of £300 is required at final balance payment.

Force majeure: In the event of cancellation by Elmhurst Estate due to circumstances beyond our control, all payments will be refunded within 28 days.

Elmhurst Estate Management

documents.title: Elmhurst Estate – Old Cancellation Policy (Jan 2024)
documents.content:
Cancellation & Damage Policy — January 2024

Cancellations more than 60 days prior to the event: 50% deposit refund.
Cancellations within 60 days: deposit forfeited.

A damage bond of £200 is payable on arrival.

Note: This document was issued to all clients booking in 2024. Please contact us if you have any questions.

Elmhurst Estate Management

Late payment attracts a £5 surcharge after 14 February.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 2 (Bramble), 9 June 2024
documents.content:
Hive 2 – Bramble colony. Inspected 9/6/24, weather sunny, ~21°C.

Frames 1–4: good brood pattern, capped honey on outer frames. Frame 5: spotted one charged queen cell – tore it down. Queen seen on frame 3, laying well. Temper: calm, no smoke needed after initial puff. Varroa board count over 48 hrs: 6 mites. No signs of AFB or EFB. Hefted hive – feels heavy, no feeding needed. Next inspection due in 7 days (i.e. 16 June).

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 1 (Orchard), 8 June 2024
documents.content:
Hive 1 – Orchard colony. Sat 8 June 2024.

General condition good. Queen located on frame 6 – marked with white dot (2021 queen). Brood: some scattered pattern on frame 4, worth watching. No queen cells found. Stores: moderate, may need feeding if flow stops. Varroa drop (72 hrs): 14 mites – borderline, consider treatment in July. Temper a bit grumpy today, used more smoke than usual. Population looks strong going into summer. Next check: around 22nd June.

documents.title: Mandatory Training Policy – Infection Control (v2, Current)
documents.content:
Policy no.: IC-114 v2 | Effective: 1 March 2024
All clinical staff must complete the online Infection Control refresher annually. Completion deadline is 31 May each year. Staff who have not completed by the deadline will be removed from the schedule until compliance is confirmed. This version replaces IC-114 v1 (effective June 2022) which set a 30 June deadline. Contact the compliance team at compliance@generalhosp.org for access codes.

documents.title: Mandatory Training Policy – Infection Control (v1, Superseded)
documents.content:

Staff who have not completed by the deadline will be removed from the schedule until compliance is confirmed. This version replaces IC-114 v1 (effective June 2022) which set a 30 June deadline. The earlier deadline of 31 May was introduced to align with accreditation review timing. Time allowed for the module: 90 minutes. Contact the compliance team at compliance@generalhosp.org for access codes.

documents.title: Mandatory Training Policy – Infection Control (v1, Superseded)

documents.title: Employer Relocation Policy – Vantara BV (Effective 1 Jan 2025)
documents.content:
Relocation Support Policy — effective 1 January 2025

Eligible employees relocating from outside the EU will receive a one-time relocation allowance of EUR 2,500, paid with the first Dutch payroll. Receipted shipping costs are reimbursable up to EUR 3,500. Hotel accommodation is covered for up to 14 nights at a rate not exceeding EUR 110 per night. A temporary housing allowance of EUR 400 per month is payable for the first three months. Employees must submit all receipts within 90 days of the official start date. Visa and immigration legal fees are fully reimbursable with prior approval. Policy document: VB-HR-POL-2025-003.

documents.title: Employer Relocation Policy – Vantara BV (Superseded, 2023 version)
documents.content:
Relocation Support Policy — effective 1 March 2023

Eligible employees relocating internationally will receive a one-time relocation allowance of EUR 1,800, paid with first payroll. Receipted shipping costs reimbursable up to EUR 2,800. Hotel accommodation covered for up to 10 nights, not exceeding EUR 95 per night. Temporary housing allowance: EUR 300 per month for first three months. Receipts must be submitted within 60 days of start date. Immigration legal fees reimbursable with prior approval. This policy applies to all offers made before 31 December 2024. Policy document: VB-HR-POL-2023-011.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 1, First Inspection
documents.content:
Date: May 6 2023 — Hive 1 (south garden, near the fence)
Weather: sunny, 68°F, light breeze
Frames inspected: 8 of 10
Queen spotted: yes, good laying pattern
Brood: 4 frames capped, 1 frame open
Honey stores: 1.5 frames
Pests: no visible varroa on bees; didn't do a wash yet
Mood: calm, minimal bearding
Notes: Everything looks healthy for a new install. Will add a super once 6–7 frames are drawn. Next inspection planned in ~3 weeks.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 2, First Inspection
documents.content:
May 6, 2023 — Hive 2 (north side, beside the shed)
Weather same as Hive 1 notes.
Frames inspected: 7 of 10
Queen: not spotted but eggs present — she's in there
Brood: 2 frames capped, 2 open
Honey: about 1 frame
Pests: one beetle trap set, no hive beetles found
Temperament: slightly defensive, got one sting through glove on right hand
Notes: Behind Hive 1 development-wise. Keep watching for queen. Consider combining if no improvement by June.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 1, Second Inspection
documents.content:
27 May 2023
Hive 1 — south garden
Queen seen again, beautiful brood pattern, 6 full frames brood now
Honey: 3 frames — went ahead and added the medium super today
Varroa alcohol wash: 3 mites per 100 bees (below treatment threshold)
Mood: very calm, almost no smoke needed
Weight (heft test): noticeably heavier than May 6
Next inspection: ~June 17

documents.title: Incident Post-Mortem Notes – 9 Aug 2024
documents.content:
Incident: database failover triggered unexpectedly at 02:17 UTC, lasted approx 23 minutes.

On-call at time: Priya Nair (correctly per rota). Escalated to Marcus at 02:31 UTC after automated recovery failed.

Root cause: a stale read replica DNS entry that wasn't cleared after last month's migration. The fix was a one-liner but required prod access.

Action items:
1. Add replica DNS cleanup to the migration runbook (owner: Rashida, due 23 Aug).
2. Review prod-access policy – current policy requires a second approver for any direct DB command; neither engineer on the call had reviewed whether this was waivable in a P1. Needs clarification.
3. Schedule a 30-min retro with the full team week of 19 Aug.

Draft reviewed by Tom. Not yet circulated to stakeholders.

documents.title: Production Access Policy v1.1 (Superseded – see v1.2)
documents.content:
Policy: Production Database Access
Version 1.1 – Effective 1 January 2024

Any engineer requiring direct access to a production database must:
1. Raise a change request ticket at least 2 business days in advance.
2. Obtain approval from their team lead.
3. Execute changes only during the approved maintenance window (Tuesdays and Thursdays, 22:00–02:00 UTC).

Emergency (P1) exceptions: a single approver (the on-call engineer's direct manager) may grant immediate access. Access must be revoked within 4 hours and a post-mortem filed within 48 hours.

This version is superseded. Do not use for compliance purposes.

documents.title: Production Access Policy v1.2 (Current)
documents.content:
Policy: Production Database Access
Version 1.2 – Effective 1 June 2024

Any engineer requiring direct access to a production database must:
1. Raise a change request ticket at least 2 business days in advance.
2. Obtain approval from their team lead AND a second approver (security team rep).
3. Execute changes only during the approved maintenance window (Tuesdays and Thursdays, 22:00–02:00 UTC).

Emergency (P1) exceptions: two approvers are now required even in a P1 – team lead plus any available senior engineer. Access must be revoked within 2 hours and a post-mortem filed within 24 hours.

Note: the post-mortem filing window was shortened from 48 h (v1.1) to 24 h in this revision. Version 1.1 is no longer valid.

Day 2, 19 Sep: 09:00 retrospective. 11:00 break-out groups. Wrap by 14:00; rooms must be vacated by 11:00 so store luggage at front desk.

Travel budget per person: £185 (rail + taxi). Receipts required for reimbursement; submit to Accounts by 27 September.

documents.title: Travel Reimbursement Policy v1.2 (SUPERSEDED)
documents.content: Effective January 1, 2023. Staff may claim up to $180 per night for hotel accommodation during approved conference travel. Meals are reimbursed at a flat rate of $45 per day. Ground transportation (taxi, rideshare, transit) is reimbursable up to $60 per trip. All receipts must be submitted within 30 days of return. International travel requires pre-approval from the department head at least 6 weeks in advance. This version superseded by v1.3 issued March 2024.

documents.title: Travel Reimbursement Policy v1.3 (CURRENT)
documents.content: Effective 1 March 2024. Hotel accommodation: up to $210/night for domestic travel, $260/night for international. Meal per diem is $55/day. Ground transportation reimbursable up to $75 per trip. Receipts must be submitted no later than 45 days after return. International travel requires department head pre-approval a minimum of 6 weeks before departure. Airfare must be economy class unless a journey exceeds 6 hours, in which case premium economy is permitted. Direct booking through the university portal is strongly encouraged.

documents.title: Email: NeurIPS 2024 Invitation to Review

Dear Dr. Okonkwo,

We would like to invite you to serve as a reviewer for NeurIPS 2024. Your expertise in probabilistic graphical models makes you an excellent fit for our program. The review deadline is 2 October 2024. Please confirm your availability by 25 August 2024. Reviewers who complete all assignments on time will receive a free registration code. We hope you can join us.

Best,
NeurIPS 2024 Program Chairs

NeurIPS 2024 Program Chairs

NeurIPS 2024 — Vancouver, Dec 9–13

Mon 9: Arrive ~6pm, check in Westin. Evening: workshop dinner (self-pay)
Tue 10: Tutorial day — Causal Inference in LLMs 9am, Diffusion Models 2pm
Wed 11: Main conference opens. My poster session 4–6pm (poster #317)
Thu 12: Panel on responsible AI 10am. Dinner with Santiago and the UCL group, ~7pm (expense this?)
Fri 13: Half day, checkout by noon, flight home 3:45pm

Remember: pick up badge Mon evening if registration desk open late

documents.title: Email: Reimbursement Submission Reminder from Dept Admin
documents.content:
From: finance-admin@westernridge.edu
To: m.okonkwo@westernridge.edu
Date: December 16, 2024

Hi Miriam,

Just a reminder that all receipts and the completed ER-7 form for your Vancouver trip should be submitted to me no later than 45 days from the date of return. Your return date on file is Dec 13, so the deadline would be January 27, 2025. Please attach original receipts (scans accepted) and note the grant code for any expenditure over $500. Give me a shout if you have questions!

Cheers,
Dept Finance Admin

documents.title: Personal Note – Reimbursement Checklist
documents.content:
Things to claim for Vancouver trip:
- Flights: $618.40 (+ $24 seat selection = $642.40 total airfare)
- Hotel: 4 nights @ $245 CAD — need to submit Westin folio once I check out
- Meals: 5 days × $55 = $275 (per diem, no receipts needed per new policy)
- Airport taxi home: ~$52, paid cash — wrote note on back of receipt
- Do NOT claim registration — using free reviewer code, will get refund on p-card

Total estimated (excl. hotel): $642.40 + $275 + $52 = approx $969.40 CAD before hotel

documents.title: Travel Reimbursement Policy v1.2 (SUPERSEDED)
documents.content: Effective January 1, 2023. Staff may claim up to $180 per night for hotel accommodation during approved conference travel. Meals are reimbursed at a flat rate of $45 per day. Ground transportation (taxi, rideshare, transit) is reimbursable up to $60 per trip. All receipts must be submitted within 30 days of return. International travel requires pre-approval from the department head at least 6 weeks in advance. This version superseded by v1.3 issued March 2024.

documents.title: Travel Reimbursement Policy v1.3 (CURRENT)
documents.content: Effective 1 March 2024. Hotel accommodation: up to $210/night for domestic travel, $260/night for international. Meal per diem is $55/day. Ground transportation reimbursable up to $75 per trip. Receipts must be submitted no later than 45 days after return. International travel requires department head pre-approval a minimum of 6 weeks before departure. Airfare must be economy class unless a journey exceeds 6 hours, in which case premium economy is permitted. Direct booking through the university portal is strongly encouraged.

Ridgewood Amateur Beekeepers Association – Membership Rules (adopted March 2021)

Annual dues are $45 per household. Members must register all hive locations with the county extension office within 30 days of installing a new colony. Guests may attend up to two meetings before joining. Dues are payable by 1 February each year.

Annual dues are $55 per household, effective from the 2023 renewal cycle. Members must register all hive locations with the county extension office within 30 days of installing a new colony. Hive inspection logs must be submitted digitally via the member portal by the end of each quarter. Swarm calls are to be reported to the swarm coordinator within 12 hours. Guests may attend up to three meetings before joining. Dues are payable by 15 January each year. This version supersedes all prior editions.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 1, 14 May 2023
documents.content:
Inspection – Hive 1 (back garden, near the fence)
Date: 14 May 2023, about 2pm, sunny, 72°F

Queen spotted on frame 4 – good laying pattern, nice solid brood. Saw maybe 8 frames of bees, strong colony. No signs of varroa on wash but didn't do a full alcohol wash today. Two capped queen cells on frame 7 – not sure if they're planning to swarm or just supersedure. Added a medium super on top since the nectar flow seems to have started. Noted some burr comb between boxes, scraped off. Will check again in 10 days.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 2, 14 May 2023
documents.content:
Inspection – Hive 2 (side yard)
Date: May 14 2023, same afternoon as Hive 1

Couldn't find the queen but saw fresh eggs so she's in there somewhere. Brood pattern looks a bit spotty – maybe 60% capped, rest open. Population seems lower than Hive 1. Found 3 dead bees at entrance with deformed wings – possible DWV, should do a varroa wash next visit. One frame had some chalk brood in the corners. No extra space needed yet. Will treat with oxalic acid if wash confirms mite load over 2%.

Hi all,

Just a quick note – we've had to move the Spring Picnic from May 20th to June 3rd. The pavilion at Creekside Park was double-booked; I'm really sorry for the short notice. Everything else stays the same: potluck format, bring a dish to share, starts at noon. Margaret will be doing the beginner hive demo around 1:30.

Please update your calendars. If you already have a conflict on June 3rd just let me know.

Cheers,
Margaret

documents.title: Personal Note – Queen Purchase Plan
documents.content:
Reminder to self – queen situation
written: sometime in late May 2023

Need to order a replacement Italian queen for Hive 2 given the spotty brood. Checked Kelley Bees – marked Italian queens are $32 each plus $8 shipping. Mann Lake has them for $29 but shipping is $12, so same ballpark. Thinking I'll go with Kelley just for the marking and familiarity. Need to order before the end of June or stock runs out. Also: don't forget the hive tool is getting rusty – should grab a new J-hook hive tool next time I'm placing an order anywhere.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 1, 14 May 2023
documents.content:
Inspection – Hive 1 (back garden, near the fence)
Date: 14 May 2023, about 2pm, sunny, 72°F

Queen spotted on frame 4 – good laying pattern, nice solid brood. Saw maybe 8 frames of bees, strong colony. No signs of varroa on wash but didn't do a full alcohol wash today. Two capped queen cells on frame 7 – not sure if they're planning to swarm or just supersedure. Added a medium super on top since the nectar flow seems to have started. Noted some burr comb between boxes, scraped off. Will check again in 10 days.

documents.title: Hive Inspection Notes – Hive 2, 14 May 2023
documents.content:
Inspection – Hive 2 (side yard)
Date: May 14 2023, same afternoon as Hive 1

Couldn't find the queen but saw fresh eggs so she's in there somewhere. Brood pattern looks a bit spotty – maybe 60% capped, rest open. Population seems lower than Hive 1. Found 3 dead bees at entrance with deformed wings – possible DWV, should do a varroa wash next visit. One frame had some chalk brood in the corners. No extra space needed yet. Will treat with oxalic acid if wash confirms mite load over 2%.

The Larches Surgery, 4 Elm Row, Bristol BS6 7TT

11th April 2024

This letter confirms that Zoe Fortescue (DOB 03/09/2012) has a diagnosis of mild intermittent asthma. She requires a Salbutamol inhaler (100 mcg, 2 puffs as needed) to be kept accessible at all times, including during school trips and travel abroad.

Yours sincerely,
Dr P. Mehta

documents.title: Greenvale Academy – Medication in School Policy (2022 version – superseded)
documents.content:
Greenvale Academy — Administration of Medicines Policy
Approved by Governors: September 2022

Parents wishing to have prescription medication kept on school premises must complete Form MED-1 and supply a signed letter from a GP or pharmacist. Inhalers may be held by the class teacher in a locked cupboard. Self-administration by pupils is not permitted without a separate risk assessment signed by the Head of Year.

This policy was reviewed in January 2024. Please ensure you are reading the current version. (See Jan 2024 update.)

documents.title: Greenvale Academy – Medication in School Policy (current, Jan 2024)
documents.content:
Greenvale Academy — Administration of Medicines Policy
Approved by Governors: January 2024

Parents wishing to have prescription medication kept on school premises must complete Form MED-2 (updated from MED-1) and supply a signed letter from a GP or pharmacist. Pupils in Year 5 and above may self-administer reliever inhalers after a one-off assessment completed with the school nurse. Inhalers should be stored in the pupil's school bag, not in a locked cupboard. The school nurse holds a salbutamol emergency inhaler for general use.

For trips and residentials, a copy of the GP letter must accompany the health form submitted to the school office.

documents.content:
Greenvale Academy — Administration of Medicines Policy
Approved by Governors: September 2022

Parents wishing to have prescription medication kept on school premises must complete Form MED-1 and supply a signed letter from a GP or pharmacist. Inhalers may be held by the class teacher in a locked cupboard. Self-administration by pupils is not permitted without a separate risk assessment signed by the Head of Year.

This policy was reviewed in January 2024. Please ensure you are reading the current version. (See Jan 2024 update.)

documents.title: Greenvale Academy – Medication in School Policy (current, Jan 2024)
documents.content:
Greenvale Academy — Administration of Medicines Policy
Approved by Governors: January 2024

Parents wishing to have prescription medication kept on school premises must complete Form MED-2 (updated from MED-1) and supply a signed letter from a GP or pharmacist. Pupils in Year 5 and above may self-administer reliever inhalers after a one-off assessment completed with the school nurse. Inhalers should be stored in the pupil's school bag, not in a locked cupboard. The school nurse holds a salbutamol emergency inhaler for general use.

For trips and residentials, a copy of the GP letter must accompany the health form submitted to the school office.
